A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 19-page versions of ARF-RLHF. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original satisfaction-scoring results, preference-tracking experiments, RLHF comparisons, ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds HH-RLHF evaluation and an analysis of disagreement among sentiment-labeling models.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the stated stopping condition from accumulated context length exceeding Lmax to generated-response length exceeding Lmax. The scorers, preference fusion, replay mechanism and DAM objective are retained; expanded scoring instructions largely clarify the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds human-annotated HH-RLHF evaluation, substantially extending RLHF validation beyond the retained constructed and DeepSeek-labeled preference experiments. The existing QA tasks, sentiment datasets and Emotion3 coverage remain.

E2.justification: KTO becomes an evaluated comparator alongside DPO and TraceBias in v2 Table 3. PPO, DPO and the RLAIF variants remain in their corresponding earlier comparisons. Renaming SFT to Base or Basic model does not establish another comparator.

E3.justification: The new HH-RLHF experiment combines preference scores with GPT-5 win rates against the base model. Table 8 introduces a uniformly distributed Emotion3 sample evaluation by three LLMs. Existing hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; detailed sample counts and HH-RLHF-specific settings are not supplied.

E4.justification: New Appendix G and Table 8 investigate whether GPT-4o, DeepSeek-v3 and Gemini 2.0 Flash agree on satisfaction labels, particularly neutrality. Existing ER, DAM and rescoring analyses and case studies remain; the rescoring ablation is relocated into the main text.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly reports variance across three models' sentiment-label proportions, including neutral-class variance of 29.51. This quantifies disagreement between judges, rather than uncertainty across training seeds. No confidence intervals, significance tests or additional repeated-run reporting are introduced for the main RLHF results.

E6.justification: New HH-RLHF results report DPO/KTO/TraceBias preference scores of 34.2/31.7/34.1 and GPT-5 win rates of 57%/51%/54% (Table 3). Table 8 adds sentiment-label distributions. ALPACA without rescoring changes from 7.2 to 7.8 (v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 5). Existing performance plots retain their values.

T1.justification: v2 corrects loss-sign inconsistencies in Figure 1 and Appendix B.3, including v1 Equations 41/45 versus v2 Equations 35/39. It also corrects positive-class indexing and makes cumulative trajectory bounds explicit. The PPO/DPO derivations remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims the first self-supervised RLHF framework learning satisfaction trajectories directly from free-form feedback. Performance claims broaden from v1's aggregate superiority with acknowledged exceptions to superiority across all tasks and model sizes in v2 Section 4.3. The central ARF/TraceBias contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive explanation of how neutral-dominated distributions attenuate updates (Section 5.2), interprets DPO/KTO/TraceBias performance through annotation quality, and newly asserts that DAM prevents reward hacking. These extend v1's stability explanations. The limitations concerning direct human evaluation and larger models remain.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 explicitly specifies ARF-scorer calls, and Section 4.4 identifies Qwen2.5-1.5B/GSM8K for the gradient comparison. Conversely, v1's traceStep=1 disclosure disappears. Hardware, training-time information and existing hyperparameter tables are retained, while the added experiments receive limited reproducibility details.

R1.justification: v2 substantially reframes its motivation around Common Ground Theory, LIWC and Emotion Prototype Theory, and positions ARF against preference distillation and KTO. It adds corresponding references and HH-RLHF-related positioning while removing earlier TRPO/RRHF discussion and several dataset citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, methodology and experiments are extensively rewritten. Related Work becomes Background, fusion cases are consolidated, DAM precedes trajectory scoring, and experiments are reorganized around Q1–Q3. Discussion and appendix organization also change substantially.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 8, redraws Figure 1, moves the rescoring table into the main text and relocates Figures 6–9. Those plots receive clearer visualization-scale labels without changing their values. Captions and table labels are revised, while the overall two-column format remains.

improvement.justification: The HH-RLHF comparison, supervision-disagreement analysis, clearer organization and corrected loss signs add useful evidence and clarity. However, new experiments lack detailed protocols, and the strengthened universal-superiority claim conflicts with retained Figures 7–9. Table 8 also reports negative-class variance of 13.28 although its percentages imply approximately 3.28. These gains coexist with new unsupported claims and reporting errors, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
